_about: Known floods, what river heights mean on the ground, travel times and links. Created by Josh Avard. Impact descriptions are paraphrased from the Shire of Campaspe Flood Emergency Plan, Issue 7, February 2019 (https://www.campaspe.vic.gov.au/files/assets/public/our-services/flood-emergency-plan.pdf). That plan predates the October 2022 flood and the Rochester Flood Study 2025 update, so check the latest council information.

curatedEvents.name: November 2010 flood
curatedEvents.notes: The floodplain was flooded about 200 m either side of the river, with no homes flooded over floor. It came two months before the January 2011 flood, on wet ground.

curatedEvents.name: January 2011 flood

reported.source: Campaspe Shire Flood Emergency Plan 2019 (9 pm, 16 January)

facts: About 80% of Rochester was flooded and more than 250 homes were flooded over floor.
The Campaspe at Campaspe Weir carried about 75,300 ML/day.
At Echuca, the Murray peaked about 39 hours after the Campaspe.
curatedEvents.notes: The largest flood on record at the Rochester Town gauge until October 2022.

curatedEvents.name: October 2022 flood
facts: Lake Eppalock went from 50% full on 4 August to full and spilling on 30 September.
On 13 October inflows to Eppalock jumped to a record 235,000 ML/day.
The spillway peaked at a record 103,000 ML/day on 14 October, with the lake about 134% full.
Forest, Mount Pleasant, Axe and other creeks below the dam added about 30,000 ML/day.
It was the third La Niña year in a row, with a negative Indian Ocean Dipole, and the catchment was already wet.

curatedEvents.notes: Higher than January 2011 at the Rochester Town gauge. Major flooding followed at Echuca.

curatedEvents.name: January 2024 near miss
curatedEvents.notes: The river passed the major flood level but stayed below October 2022.

rows.label: Minor flood level
rows.what: Early minor flooding. Caravan park alerted, SES patrols begin, Northern Highway pit gates closed.
Caravan park BBQ area floods. Caravans moved from the lowest level.
Caravan park amenities block floods.

rows.label: Moderate flood level
rows.what: Flooding likely in several streets and rural flooding starts. Road closures including Bridge Road, Mackay Street and the Northern Highway.
Whole caravan park evacuated.

rows.label: November 2010
rows.what: Floodplain flooded about 200 m either side of the river. No homes flooded over floor.

rows.label: Major flood level
rows.what: The old anabranch floods and water deepens along the railway.

rows.label: 1 in 10 year flood
rows.what: First 3 houses flooded over floor. Kyabram-Rochester Road and the Northern Highway may close.

rows.label: 1 in 20 year flood
rows.what: Shallow flooding east of the railway, including the hospital area.

rows.label: 1 in 50 year flood
rows.what: Shallow flooding across much of the town. About 157 properties flooded over floor.

rows.label: 1 in 100 year flood
rows.what: Flooding both sides of the railway. About 266 properties flooded over floor.

rows.label: January 2011
rows.what: About 80% of the town flooded and more than 250 homes over floor.

rows.label: October 2022
rows.what: Highest flood on record at this gauge.
Campaspe flooding shows west of the river. Campaspe Esplanade may be sandbagged.

rows.label: Minor flood level
rows.what: Early street and drain flooding. Warnings issued and some roads closed.
Flooding established west of the Campaspe and a dry island forms.

rows.label: Moderate flood level
rows.what: Regular levee patrols. Echuca East residents notified.

rows.label: 1 in 10 year flood
rows.what: Levees patrolled around the clock.
Deep flooding west of the Campaspe. Evacuation of Crescent and Bynan streets considered.

rows.label: Major flood level
rows.what: The Campaspe reaches the backs of properties. Temporary levees or sandbagging considered.

rows.label: October 1993
rows.what: Largest flood since 1975 at this gauge.
Lowest point in the town levees (Watson Street).
General design height of the levees.

rows.label: 1 in 100 year flood
rows.what: Moving shire offices and police considered.

rows.label: November 1870
rows.what: Flood of record. Extensive flooding and the town water supply at risk.
